title: Ledger Concurrency Substrate (Single-Writer-by-Construction)
intent: gzkit cannot safely run more than one agent at a time against the same repository because the system-of-record is not concurrency-safe. `.gzkit/ledger.jsonl` is an append-only file written on the single-writer assumption, and the OBPI-lock system (`.gzkit/locks/`) is advisory. Two agents working concurrently — e.g. two worktrees both reaching `gz obpi complete` — would interleave writes to Layer-2, corrupting the append-only invariant the whole trust model rests on. This pool ADR captures the enabling invariant that any write-heavy multi-agent parallelism (see ADR-pool.worktree-parallel-agents) must sit on. It is deliberately the substrate, not the feature: it makes concurrent Layer-2 mutation impossible-by-construction rather than merely coordinated.
decision:
Adopt SINGLE-WRITER-BY-CONSTRUCTION for the ledger, with NO resident daemon.

1. Parallel/worktree agents write ZERO Layer-2 ledger events during their parallel phase. Their output is code, findings, and worktree-local artifacts only.
2. The only surface that appends to `.gzkit/ledger.jsonl` is the serialized merge-to-main step. Concurrency is resolved by construction: there is exactly one writer because there is exactly one merge lane (main).
3. This is not a new invariant — it makes an existing architectural boundary load-bearing: Architectural Boundaries §6 and state-doctrine already hold that derived views are Layer-3 and that Layer-2 facts originate from governed writes. Here we add: parallel work is Layer-3 scratch until it merges; only the merge writes Layer-2.
4. No `handoffd`-style daemon. swarm-forge needs a daemon because tmux is a shared live socket that every agent must reach concurrently; gzkit's ledger is a file whose writes can be funnelled through a single logical lane (merge) without a resident process. Choosing the daemon would incur stdlib-first cost (a long-lived process, lifecycle, failure modes) to solve a problem the merge-lane funnel already solves.
positive_consequences:
1. Concurrent ledger corruption becomes impossible-by-construction, not merely discouraged by advisory locks.
2. Unblocks the write-heavy modes of ADR-pool.worktree-parallel-agents (parallel OBPI implementation, parallel GHI fixes) without inventing a distributed-write protocol.
3. Zero new runtime machinery: no daemon, no lockservice, no external store. Honors STDLIB-FIRST.
4. Preserves the append-only ledger as the untouched system-of-record; parallelism happens entirely in Layer-3 scratch.
5. Reuses the existing merge-to-main discipline the operator already mandates ('everything lands on main') as the serialization point — the funnel already exists.
negative_consequences:
1. Parallel agents cannot emit progress/telemetry events to the shared ledger mid-flight — their governance footprint is invisible until merge. This is a real observability cost for long parallel runs.
2. The merge step becomes a heavier, all-or-nothing accounting transaction (it must replay/emit every deferred Layer-2 event for the merged work). Merge-time failure handling needs design.
3. Ordering: if two parallel units both must record events, the merge lane serializes them, so their ledger timestamps reflect merge order, not work order. Any consumer that reasons about work-order from ledger-order must be audited.
4. Does not by itself make the OBPI-lock system non-advisory; it sidesteps the race rather than hardening the lock. If a future mode genuinely needs mid-flight Layer-2 writes, this substrate does not cover it and the daemon question reopens.
5. Introduces a new implicit rule ('parallel work is Layer-3 until merge') that must be taught and gated, or it silently decays.
checklist:
1. Formalize the invariant: 'during parallel/worktree work no process other than the merge-to-main lane appends to `.gzkit/ledger.jsonl`' — as a named boundary in state-doctrine.
2. Define the merge-lane accounting transaction: how deferred Layer-2 events for merged work are emitted atomically at merge time.
3. Define failure/recovery behavior for a merge that fails partway through emitting deferred events (all-or-nothing; leave the worktree for retry).
4. A validator that fail-closes if a Layer-2 event is emitted from a worktree/parallel context outside the merge lane.
5. Decide whether advisory OBPI-locks are retired, kept as a courtesy signal, or upgraded to worktree-scoped — in light of the by-construction guarantee.
alternatives:
1. Daemon-owned ledger writer (direct swarm-forge `handoffd` analog): a single long-lived process owns `.gzkit/ledger.jsonl`; parallel agents enqueue events it serializes. REJECTED for pool-default: most faithful to swarm-forge but adds a resident process and its lifecycle/failure surface — a STDLIB-FIRST departure that must be foundation-attested, and the merge-lane funnel already achieves serialization without it. Kept on record as the fallback IF a future mode needs mid-flight Layer-2 writes.
2. Advisory worktree-scoped locks only: extend the existing OBPI-lock system to worktree scope and rely on cooperation. REJECTED: cheapest, but locks remain advisory — it leaves exactly the race window this ADR exists to close.
3. External transactional store (SQLite/Dolt) for the ledger: REJECTED as over-reach and a direct contradiction of the append-only-JSONL system-of-record and ADR-pool.storage-simplicity-profile posture.
pre_mortem: 18 months on, this failed because the 'no Layer-2 writes until merge' rule was never mechanically gated, so an agent emitted a completion event from a worktree, the merge lane re-emitted it, and the ledger carried a duplicate attested completion nobody caught — the exact silent-corruption class the append-only invariant exists to prevent. Mitigation: checklist item 4 (fail-closed validator) is not optional.
wwhtbt: For single-writer-by-construction to be right, it must be true that no legitimate parallel mode needs to record a Layer-2 fact before merge. Shakiest condition: a long parallel run that an operator wants to observe mid-flight — if that need is real and frequent, the daemon alternative wins. It is currently judged rare because the primary use case (parallel review personas) is read-only and write-free.
reversibility: Two-way door. If the by-construction funnel proves too restrictive, the daemon alternative can be adopted later without unwinding this — the merge lane simply becomes one client of the daemon. Low reversal cost keeps this the right first move.
operator_2am: On-call at 2am a parallel merge half-emitted its deferred events and aborted. The operator needs: a single command that reports which worktrees have unmerged/unaccounted work, and a guarantee the ledger was left consistent (no partial event set). Checklist item 3 owes this.
scope_minimization: Smallest valuable version: the named invariant + the fail-closed validator (checklist 1 and 4), with the merge-accounting transaction (2,3) deferred until a write-heavy mode is actually promoted. That alone makes the read-only parallel-review capability safe to land.
downstream_adrs: Forces ADR-pool.worktree-parallel-agents (the capability that consumes this). May force a state-doctrine amendment naming the parallel=Layer-3-until-merge boundary, and a validator ADR if the fail-closed check grows beyond a stub.
